request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change that moves anyone's claimed or due-total now adds ROLLUP lines to the audit, then a TOTALS line if a sheet total moved. `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec, including the three extra scenarios.

**How it works:** before a change runs, the server snapshots each person's claimed and due-total and the sheet's two totals. After the change's own audit line, it takes the snapshot again and compares the two:
- **ROLLUP:** one line per person whose figures differ, in the order they were added. Someone who didn't exist before counts as changed, and a due-total with no rate is written as `n/a`.
- **TOTALS:** one line, only when the claimed-total or due-total changed.
- **No figure moved:** no lines at all. That covers re-setting a rate to its current value, settling a claim at its live figure, and a statement that changes nothing.
- **Refused changes:** nothing is recorded, because the recording step never runs.

The spec writes the person's name as `person=<name>`, not the `name=<name>` the request text gave, so I used `person=`.

**Where the changes are:**
- **New code** in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`:
  - `Rollup.java` works out the figures the same way the screen does.
  - `TakeRollup.java` takes the snapshot before the change.
  - `RecordRollup.java` compares and writes the lines.
- **Wiring:** both steps are added to all ten write endpoints under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/`: add/edit person, statement, add claim, edit claim, open/settle/void claim, set rate, and change today. Changing today writes only these lines, with no line of its own.
- **No front-end or database changes** were needed.

The figure calculation now exists twice, in `Rollup.java` and in the front end's `features/rates/api.ts`. If one changes and the other doesn't, the audit and the screen will disagree.
